title: Charles Duncan Buried with Honor Act of 2016
official_summary:
(This measure has not been amended since it was passed by the Senate on September 20, 2016. The summary of that version is repeated here.)

Charles Duncan Buried with Honor Act of 2016

(Sec. 2) This bill authorizes the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), if it is unable to identify a deceased veteran's next of kin and if it determines that sufficient resources for the furnishing of a casket or urn for the burial of such veteran are not otherwise available, to furnish a casket or urn for the burial of such veteran in a national cemetery (current law) or in a veterans cemetery of a state or tribal organization for which the VA has provided a grant for the establishment, expansion, and improvement of veterans' cemeteries.

summary.headline: A new law lets the VA provide a casket or urn for certain veterans whose next of kin cannot be found, for burial in national or grant-supported state or tribal veterans cemeteries.
summary.what_it_does: The law allows the Department of Veterans Affairs to pay for a casket or urn when it cannot identify a deceased veteran's next of kin. It applies only if other resources for the casket or urn are not available. The burial can be in a VA national cemetery or in a state or tribal veterans cemetery that received a VA grant to establish, expand, or improve it.

who_it_affects.group: Deceased veterans with no identifiable next of kin
who_it_affects.how: Their burial may include a casket or urn furnished by the VA when other resources are not available.

who_it_affects.group: State and tribal veterans cemeteries that received VA grants
who_it_affects.how: They may be used as burial sites for veterans whose caskets or urns the VA furnishes.
The agency gains authority to furnish caskets or urns in these situations.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The law became effective upon enactment on December 14, 2016.
